headline: Drugmaker Eli Lilly and AI company insitro opened their drug-behavior prediction models to selected biotech firms on Lilly's TuneLab platform.
score_reason: Company announcement with a real access change for biotechs, but claims are insitro's own and no outside results are given.
importance_line: Early-stage drug developers, especially smaller biotechs, gain access to prediction tools built on decades of Lilly data, but the benefit is the companies' own claim and has not been independently tested.
source: insitro press release, as carried by BioSpace
summary: insitro, an AI company focused on drug discovery, said in a press release that machine-learning models it built with Eli Lilly to predict how small-molecule drug candidates behave in the body can now be used by certain biotech companies on Lilly's TuneLab platform. The models were trained on decades of Lilly's animal and lab data from hundreds of thousands of molecules, and insitro says they could help weed out weak candidates before they are made, although the company has not published outside testing.
notes: Original Dealroom page blocked; read insitro's press release on BioSpace.
